newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says wheat crop down by a million tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Iran says wheat crop down by a million tonnes.

text.p: Iran's wheat production fell in the last crop year by a million tonnes because of bad weather and lower cultivated acreage, a senior official said in a statement published on Monday.

Behrouz Qahraman of the agriculture ministry said in a statement published in the daily Kayhan that growers had sold less wheat to the government at fixed prices, finding it more profitable to sell their crop as animal feed on the open market.

Qahraman, head of the ministry's office for wheat, rice and grains, was answering questions by the newspaper on Iran's wheat imports which are expected to reach 6.6 million tonnes in the year to June 30, making it the world's biggest importer.
"In (the last) crop year wheat production showed a decrease of more than a million tonnes compared to the previous year," Qahraman said. He did not say when the crop year ended.
Lower rainfall in many regions, coupled with rain during harvest or too much rain in other areas, damaged the wheat crop, the official said.
Land used for wheat cultivation had decreased because it was more profitable to grow other crops, Qahraman said. He did not give figures for acreage loss or last year's total output.
Kayhan said the production fall was also due to the government's buying price of 480 rials (16 U.S. cents) per kg being too low.
Iran's government buys wheat from farmers at prices it sets. It then sells the wheat to bakeries for production of bread which is sold at heavily subsidised prices.
Iran said in April it would import five million tonnes of wheat in addition to buying another five million tonnes from local producers in the current Iranian year which ends on March 20, 1998.
Officials said the government would pay a total of six trillion rials ($2 billion) for the wheat purchases.
Bread is a main staple of the Iranian diet and among commodities for which the government has budgeted to pay $1.4 billion in subsidies in the current Iranian year.
($1=3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
